## A. Merge queue — DRAINED 2026-10-17

Zero open PRs. `main` at `acddb39`. Merged in this pass: **#87** S3-03 · **#89** S4-05 · **#92** S7-02 ·
**#98** S2-09 boot · **#100** gate username · **#101** S2-09 work. Earlier the same day: #91/#93 S1-09,
#96/#97 S2-08, #99 S1-08 addendum.

**Two things learned here, recorded because they cost real time:**
- `gh pr update-branch && gh pr merge` **chained with `&&` can never work.** The update creates a new
  head whose required `CI` has not started, so the merge a second later always fails. They are two
  actions with a ~3 minute gap.
- The ruleset's `strict_required_status_checks_policy` (require branches up to date) turns a queue of
  N memory-touching PRs into N sequential update→wait→merge cycles, because **every merge invalidates
  every other PR.** It was switched off deliberately to drain this queue. **→ OWNER ACTION: switch it
  back on** at https://github.com/shorobot/shosho/settings/rules/23652140 — Rules → `main-protection` →
  Require status checks to pass → tick "Require branches to be up to date before merging". The queue is
  drained, so the reason for having it off is gone.
- Conflict resolution across sibling reports is **not** one blanket rule. `memory/log.md` is append-only
  → keep both sides. `memory/state.md` is **per row**: take `main`'s rows for other sessions and the
  branch's own row from the branch, because only that session may write its row — three times a whole-side
  choice would have reverted another session's progress or discarded the author's own report.
  `docs/security.md` needed opposite calls in two hunks of the same file: one side was a stale finding the
  PR existed to correct (take the PR's), the other was two unrelated pieces of S7 work (take both).

## D-bis. Consequence of Option A that must be chosen, not inherited
`/kitchen` and `/driver` exist as real screens behind the **same** outer gate as `/orders`. If the basic-auth pair is known to two people, kitchen staff and drivers cannot reach their own screens at all — and S7-02 spent a whole boot auditing kitchen's RLS reach, which only matters if kitchen can log in.

This does **not** force distributing the pair. Basic-auth is device-bound in practice: the browser caches it. So the owner enters the pair **once** on the kitchen tablet and on the driver's phone, and those people then use their own staff logins inside the app. Four roles work; two people know the secret. Known costs: the cache is lost to a site-data clear, a private window, and sometimes a browser update — each time the owner must re-enter it; and a lost device is a leaked pair, so it means rotation.

**Owner chose A2 on 2026-10-16: per-device setup.** The owner enters the pair once on the kitchen tablet and the driver's phone; those people then use their own staff logins inside. Four roles work, two people know the secret.

**This promotes B4 and B5 from theoretical to live exposure, and that is the main consequence of the choice.** While kitchen could not pass the outer gate at all, their reach was academic. Under A2 a kitchen tablet holds a working kitchen session, sits in a kitchen, is probably shared between shifts and probably stays logged in — so what a kitchen login can reach is now a real question with two known-wrong answers: `orders_kitchen_read` is unbounded (**every order ever placed**, readable from the kitchen tablet) and `settings.draft` leaks to kitchen/driver (**unpublished website content**, same place). Neither is catastrophic; both are now worth fixing before the tablets go out rather than after.
